chunks: From him, from Abdullah, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Nuh ibn Darradj, who said:

I said to Ibn Abi Layla: 'Did you leave a statement you had made, or a judgment you had rendered, because of the statement of anyone?' He said: 'No, except for one man.' I said: 'Who is he?' He said: 'Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.ابْنُ أَبِي لَيْلَى: Ibn Abi Layla, a prominent early jurist and judge
key_terms.جَعْفَرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ: Ja'far ibn Muhammad, the sixth Imam, known as Al-Sadiq

ai.seo_question: Who was the single person whose statement caused Ibn Abi Layla to reverse his legal judgments?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the profound scholarly deference of the prominent Meccan jurist Ibn Abi Layla to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, acknowledging his authority even over his own established rulings. It underscores the Shia principle of recognizing the infallible Imam's legal expertise, where his word carries the weight of finality in matters of jurisprudence. This narrative serves as a key evidence for the high status of the Ahl al-Bayt in the broader Islamic scholarly tradition.
